doc.title: Johnny Varro interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clearwater Beach, Florida, March 16, 2001

title: Bobby Hackett as teacher and musician
summary: Hackett's harmonic knowledge and teaching; upcoming tribute concert.

story.theme_name: Remembering the early trumpeters and their styles
story.community_name: Trumpeters I admired: rating the horn players

blocks.x: Of course Bobby, he knew, as you said, he knew chords, he used to play guitar too.
So he really knew his harmony and all that.

Yes he did that’s very true. He’s one of the few in those days that did, of the horn players. Horn players, most of them played by instinct, by ear, by hearing. But Bobby knew his changes. And like some of these other guys just played — I mean they did just as well in a lot of cases. But Bobby’s harmonies were so great. He knew — he’d sometimes hit that third on the bottom and then go the rest of the chord up. He was a great teacher. A great influence.
Oh Jesus man, he was beautiful. We are doing a concert next month in Gainesville, a tribute to Bobby. So it should be fun.
